holidays.name: National Parfait Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the layered dessert of yogurt, fruit, granola, or ice cream stacked in a tall glass. Spoon all the way down to hit every layer.
holidays.origin: Like many food observances, it is an unofficial holiday popularized through food calendars. The word parfait is French for 'perfect', and the dessert dates to 19th-century France, where it was a frozen custard-style dish.
holidays.funFact: The original French parfait was a smooth frozen dessert made with egg yolks, sugar syrup, and cream. The layered American version with granola and yogurt came much later.

holidays.name: International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women
holidays.description: A serious UN-designated day of awareness and action. Landmarks around the world are lit up in orange, and it kicks off 16 Days of Activism.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly designated November 25 in 1999. The date honors the Mirabal sisters, three activists murdered in 1960 in the Dominican Republic under dictator Rafael Trujillo.
holidays.funFact: Orange is the signature color of the campaign, symbolizing a brighter future free from violence. Buildings from the Empire State Building to pyramids have been lit orange for it.

holidays.name: Buy Nothing Day (North America)
holidays.description: A protest against consumerism where people try to go a full 24 hours without spending money, as an antidote to Black Friday shopping frenzies.
holidays.origin: Started in Vancouver in 1992 by artist Ted Dave and later promoted by Adbusters magazine. It is observed on the Friday after Thanksgiving in North America, and the following Saturday internationally. In some years that falls on November 25.
holidays.funFact: Activists have staged 'zombie walks' through shopping malls, wandering the aisles without buying a thing.

holidays.name: National Shopping Reminder Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek holiday reminding people that the holiday shopping season is in full swing and that there are only so many days left to buy gifts.
holidays.origin: This is a lighthearted unofficial observance that appears on quirky holiday calendars around the post-Thanksgiving shopping period.
holidays.funFact: Retail analysts say a large share of shoppers start holiday buying before Thanksgiving, which makes this reminder almost unnecessary.

holidays.name: Square Dance Day
holidays.description: A day for do-si-do-ing, swinging your partner, and following the caller. Grab a bandana and find a barn.
holidays.origin: Square dancing is tied to American folk culture, and the date is celebrated by dance clubs and enthusiasts as an unofficial observance. The dance has roots in English, Scottish, and French country dances brought to North America.
holidays.funFact: Square dance is the official state dance of more than 30 US states, which makes it one of the most widely adopted state symbols.
